input: The staffing ramp for the upgrade project has been set at 16%, and although a lower figure has been suggested during the review process, there are strong reasons for holding the ramp at 16% for the time being. A lower ramp is essentially based on the assumption that every post will be filled smoothly and promptly on the very day on which the previous holder leaves it, but in reality recruitment for specialist posts rarely runs in such an orderly fashion: offers are declined, notice periods overlap, and when posts are filled late, all of the packages that depend on them are held up as a consequence. The ramp is intended to cover the overlap between incoming and outgoing post holders, the periods during which posts stand empty, and the release of staff for training. Reducing the ramp would not in itself eliminate any of these gaps; it would simply transfer their cost into overtime working and into delays to dependent packages. It should also be noted that the cost table in the Costs section has been built on the 16% figure, so a change at this stage would mean reopening a large number of package estimates. It is therefore suggested that the steering group holds the figure until the actual fill rate for the first posts can be seen.
